content_units: Best-Fit Laptop Snapshot

For graduate-level data analysis, heavy browser use, Zoom, and occasional Python notebooks, all three can work, but the best   balance of battery life, performance, and 3-year comfort under EUR 1,400   is the   ASUS Zenbook 14  .
Why it stands out:
-   32GB RAM   gives the most future-proof headroom for large browser sessions, datasets, notebooks, and multitasking.
-   Ryzen 9 + 1TB SSD   gives strong overall responsiveness without paying beyond your cap.
-   1.28kg weight   is the most portable of the three.
- Its claimed battery is not the longest on paper, but still reasonable for this class.
Laptop Comparison Table
Model   Price   CPU   RAM / SSD   Weight   Claimed Battery   Best For
Lenovo Yoga Slim 7   EUR 1,199   Ryzen 7   16GB / 512GB   1.35kg   14 hours   Best value and battery-first choice
Dell Inspiron 14 Plus   EUR 1,349   Core i7   16GB / 1TB   1.60kg   9 hours   Storage-heavy workflows, less ideal for portability
ASUS Zenbook 14   EUR 1,399   Ryzen 9   32GB / 1TB   1.28kg   10 hours   Best long-term balance of power, mobility, and longevity
Ranked Recommendation
Option 1:   ASUS Zenbook 14     Best overall fit for your priorities     32GB RAM for the strongest 3-year comfort
- Best choice if you want to avoid feeling constrained by memory over time.
- Excellent for many browser tabs, Zoom, spreadsheet work, and Python notebooks running together.
- Lightest option here, which helps with daily commuting and campus use.
- Trade-off: battery is not class-leading on paper, but the extra RAM/performance is worth it for your use case.
Option 2:   Lenovo Yoga Slim 7     Best value pick with the strongest battery claim     Longest claimed battery at the lowest price
- Very good option if battery life matters more than maximum future-proofing.
- Ryzen 7 + 16GB is still fully capable for graduate work today.
- Main limitation for 3+ years:   16GB RAM and 512GB storage   may feel tighter sooner if your workflows grow.
Option 3:   Dell Inspiron 14 Plus     Solid performance and storage, but weaker fit for your priorities     Heavier with shorter claimed battery
- 1TB storage is useful, and Core i7 performance should be strong.
- But it is the   heaviest   and has the   shortest claimed battery  , which directly conflicts with your portability goal.
- Harder to justify when the ASUS is lighter and more future-ready at a similar price.
Long-Term Use Verdict
For   at least 3 years of comfortable use  , prioritize:
-   RAM first
- Then portability
- Then battery
- Then storage
That makes the recommendation:
Choose the ASUS Zenbook 14   if you want the safest all-around purchase under your budget.
Why this is the best balance for you:
-   Performance:   strongest overall spec set
-   Battery:   acceptable, even if not class-leading
-   Portability:   best in the group by weight
-   Longevity:   32GB RAM is the biggest advantage for graduate workloads over time
If you want the   best value alternative  , choose the   Lenovo Yoga Slim 7  .
Quick Actions
Pick ASUS
Check Lenovo
Buying Context
I’m comparing only the specs you provided, so the recommendation assumes:
- similar display quality and keyboard quality across models
- no unusual port, webcam, or thermal issues
- your Python use is moderate, not large local ML training or gaming
If those assumptions hold, the   ASUS Zenbook 14   is the strongest recommendation, with the   Lenovo Yoga Slim 7   as the smarter budget-conscious runner-up.
